\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{खरो} (kharo)}{खरो (kharo)}]{\mw{खरो} (kharo) — correct; genuine}

\label{lesson:MW-C271-kharo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to smash, then the Marwadi for to get cross.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{खरो}}
\textbf{\mw{खरो}} — \emph{kharo} — \textquotedblleft{}correct; genuine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{थारो} \mw{जवाब} \mw{खरो} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{thāro javāb kharo hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Your answer is correct.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{खरो}} (\emph{kharo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{khara}, \textquotedblleft{}hard, sharp\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{kharaü}, \textquotedblleft{}extreme\textquotedblright{}, Sindhi \emph{kharo}, \textquotedblleft{}pure, genuine\textquotedblright{}, and Gujarati \emph{kharũ}, \textquotedblleft{}real, good\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3819). How the sense \textquotedblleft{}correct\textquotedblright{} grew out of \textquotedblleft{}hard\textquotedblright{} is not settled. It agrees like any -\mw{ो} adjective: \textbf{\mw{खरो} \mw{जवाब}}, \textbf{\mw{खरी} \mw{बात}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kharo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kharo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thāro javāb kharo hai.} — Your answer is correct.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to smash, then the Marwadi for to get cross, then say \emph{kharo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{खरो} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Correct; genuine\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{गलत} (galat)}{गलत (galat)}]{\mw{गलत} (galat) — wrong}

\label{lesson:MW-C271-galat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to get cross, then the Marwadi for correct.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{गलत}}
\textbf{\mw{गलत}} — \emph{galat} — \textquotedblleft{}wrong\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{यो} \mw{सबद} \mw{गलत} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yo sabad galat hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This word is wrong.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{गलत}} (\emph{galat}) is usually traced, through Persian \emph{ghalat}, to Arabic \emph{ghalaṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}error\textquotedblright{}. Like \textbf{\mw{सही}}, it does not change.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{galat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yo sabad galat hai.} — This word is wrong.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to get cross, then the Marwadi for correct, then say \emph{galat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{सबूत} (sabūt)}{सबूत (sabūt)}]{\mw{सबूत} (sabūt) — proof}

\label{lesson:MW-C271-sabut}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for correct, then the Marwadi for wrong.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{सबूत}}
\textbf{\mw{सबूत}} — \emph{sabūt} — \textquotedblleft{}proof\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{सबूत} \mw{कठै} \mw{है}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sabūt kaṭhai hai?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Where's the proof?
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{सबूत}} (\emph{sabūt}) is usually traced, through Persian \emph{subūt}, to Arabic \emph{thubūt}, \textquotedblleft{}firmness; proof\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{साखी} (sākhī)}{साखी (sākhī)}]{\mw{साखी} (sākhī) — a witness}

\label{lesson:MW-C271-sakhi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for wrong, then the Marwadi for proof.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{साखी}}
\textbf{\mw{साखी}} — \emph{sākhī} — \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{राम} \mw{म्हारो} \mw{साखी} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rām mhāro sākhī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Ram is my witness.
\end{quote}

A masculine or feminine noun, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{साखी}} (\emph{sākhī}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{sākṣin}, \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{sākhī}, \textquotedblleft{}witness\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13321).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for asking and answering.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{कसम} (kasam)}{कसम (kasam)}]{\mw{कसम} (kasam) — an oath}

\label{lesson:MW-C271-kasam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for proof, then the Marwadi for a witness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{कसम}}
\textbf{\mw{कसम}} — \emph{kasam} — \textquotedblleft{}an oath\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{हूं} \mw{कसम} \mw{खाऊं} \mw{हूं}, \mw{यो} \mw{साचो} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hū̃ kasam khāū̃ hū̃, yo sācho hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I swear it: this is true.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{कसम}} (\emph{kasam}) is usually traced, through Persian \emph{qasam}, to Arabic \emph{qasam}, \textquotedblleft{}an oath\textquotedblright{}. You \textquotedblleft{}eat\textquotedblright{} an oath: \textbf{\mw{कसम} \mw{खाऊं} \mw{हूं}}, I swear.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kasam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kasam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hū̃ kasam khāū̃ hū̃, yo sācho hai.} — I swear it: this is true.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for proof, then the Marwadi for a witness, then say \emph{kasam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
